Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. videos.caption: You do not have to overcomplicate your first digital product. A simple product that solves one clear problem can be enough to get started. The key is choosing ONE specific person and ONE specific problem. Don’t just open Canva, make a random planner, and hope somebody buys it. Before you create anything, ask yourself: Who is this for? What problem are they struggling with? What would make solving that problem easier? Why would they want help with it now? Then create a simple product around that answer. It could be a guide, checklist, workbook, planner, template, tracker, or another digital resource that helps move them from the problem toward a solution. But creating the product is only part of it. You also need to learn how to: Position it so the right person understands why it’s for them. Put it somewhere they can actually purchase it. Create content that speaks to the problem they already have. And give them a clear next step when they’re interested. That’s where a lot of beginners get stuck. They create the product… Then have no idea what to do with it. That’s exactly why I created Create & Cash In.
